open_points.subject: K-08 vs M26 authority on draft-write resend
open_points.text: K-08: "a `draft-write` runs under the owner's activation of the flow instead" and "An effect resolved as not applied is sent again only with a fresh approval"; M26: "for a `draft-write` send the flow activation under which the run started ... except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records the fresh approval it needed"
open_points.question: After `not_applied`, must a `draft-write` operation require a per-attempt owner approval (despite normally using flow activation), or does `draft-write` continue to use activation only?
options: Require fresh owner approval for `draft-write` resends after `not_applied`
Keep `draft-write` under flow activation even after `not_applied`
open_points.default_guess: Require fresh owner approval for `draft-write` resends after `not_applied`, because M26 states this explicitly for all classes.

open_points.subject: StandingGrant applicability to draft-write nodes
open_points.text: Grant action failure says only: "a `destructive` node ... cannot be granted"; K-08 says only `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive` nodes stop for approval, while "a `draft-write` runs under the owner's activation of the flow instead".
open_points.question: Can a standing grant be created for a `draft-write` node, and if so does it have any authority effect or is it refused as nonsensical?
options: Allow grant on `draft-write` as a no-op record
Allow grant and treat it as authority for cases that would otherwise need fresh approval
open_points.default_guess: Refuse grant on `draft-write` nodes because they do not use per-node approval in normal execution.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt lifecycle when run is cancelled or otherwise ends with in-flight send
open_points.text: Run action: "cancel a run ... the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent"; M26 lifecycle only defines `in_flight` → `applied` | `not_applied` | `not_sent` | `unknown` and `unknown` resolution.
open_points.question: If a run is ended (`cancelled`/`refused`/`failed`) while an effect attempt is still `in_flight`, must the attempt be forced to a terminal status (and which one), or may it remain `in_flight` forever?
options: Keep `in_flight` until a transport outcome is observed even after run end
Forbid run-finalization while any attempt is `in_flight`
open_points.default_guess: Force `in_flight` to `unknown` when the run ends to preserve a closed attempt lifecycle.

open_points.subject: ProofResult persistence as product fact
open_points.text: State 0 action: "compose and prove a flow ... output ... proof result"; M17: "Persistence candidate: Not persisted; computed on demand."
open_points.question: Is a proof result at composition/activation time a stored historical fact, or only a transient recomputation that may differ later as external conditions (for example binding acceptance state) change?
options: Persist proof results per proof event
Do not persist; always recompute current proof result
Persist only latest proof result per flow version
open_points.default_guess: Do not persist and recompute on demand, following M17.

open_points.subject: M02 Slot `purpose` handling after slot creation
open_points.text: M02: "`purpose`: ... fixed when the slot is created — taken from the request that issues its first contract version, which is refused without one".
open_points.question: On later contract-authoring requests for an existing slot, is `purpose` required/allowed, and if provided with a different value is it ignored or refused?
options: Require no `purpose` after creation; refuse if present
Allow `purpose` but require exact match with existing value
open_points.default_guess: Allow `purpose` only on first contract; refuse mismatched values later.

open_points.subject: M12 Flow `purpose` handling after flow creation
open_points.text: M12: "`purpose` of a flow is fixed when the flow is created — taken from the request that composes its first version, which is refused without one".
open_points.question: On later compose requests for the same flow, is `purpose` required/allowed, and what happens if it differs from the stored one?
options: Require no `purpose` after creation; refuse if present
Allow `purpose` but require exact match with existing value
open_points.default_guess: Allow `purpose` only on first version; refuse mismatched values later.
